samples.summary: Timeout test asserts only that *a* signal exists, never that `timeoutMs` is honoured
samples.evidence: `it('bounds every request with a timeout signal')` passes `timeoutMs: 1234` but the only assertion is `expect(signal).toBeInstanceOf(AbortSignal)`. If `createImageFetcher` ignored `opts.timeoutMs` and always used `DEFAULT_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` (or any other duration), the test still passes — the option's wiring is untested, and nothing anywhere asserts a hung fetch is actually aborted. The signal's presence is real coverage; the configured duration is not.

samples.summary: The only direct unit tests for the new `seg()` primitive live in packages/core, whose vitest suite no CI lane runs
samples.evidence: `describe('seg', ...)` in packages/core/test/url.test.ts is the sole place `seg`'s encoding and dot-segment refusal are asserted head-on. Per the stated pipeline, packages/core's vitest suite is not invoked by any lane (only `tsc` via its build), so these assertions never execute in CI. Indirect coverage exists in packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts and packages/frontend/src/api/url.test.ts, which do run, so the behaviour is not wholly unverified — but the primitive's own suite is dead weight in CI.
searchedFor: grep for seg( across test dirs

samples.summary: The `seg(replace)` change in the import dry-run output has no test using a hostile id
samples.evidence: docs/notes/slides `runXImport` dry-run now prints `/documents/${seg(replace)}/content`. The existing assertions (packages/cli/test/docs-import.test.ts:356,373 — `expect(plan.path).toBe('/documents/doc-existing/content')`) use a benign id, for which `seg()` is the identity, so removing `seg()` from all three import modules would leave every test green. No test feeds a `../..`-style `--replace` id to these paths.

samples.summary: `seg(workspaceId)` in the image-upload URL is not covered by any test
samples.evidence: image-upload.test.ts calls `uploadImageFile(file, "ws-1")` and only ever asserts on the FormData body (`mock.calls[0][1]?.body`), never on the URL argument; `ws-1` is identity under `seg()` anyway. The new packages/frontend/src/api/url.test.ts enumerates every `src/api` module but omits `app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts`, so this call site could revert to raw interpolation undetected.

samples.summary: The failed-image filter added to `buildPartRelsXml` (header/footer parts) is untested
samples.evidence: The new DOCX test ('should drop an image whose fetch fails rather than failing the export') exercises only a body paragraph image and asserts on `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`. The parallel `.filter((e) => e.rId)` added to `buildPartRelsXml`, which serves header/footer image rels, has no test with a failing fetch — a regression there would produce a header rels file referencing a media file that was never written, with nothing to catch it.

samples.summary: The `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` (80-char) cap on `error.code` has no test
samples.evidence: upstream-error.test.ts covers the 500-char message cap ('caps a huge `message` on the envelope path', `'x'.repeat(5000)`) and the 4000-byte whole-body cap (`'y'.repeat(6000)`), but nothing feeds an over-long `code`; grep for `repeat(` in that file returns only the message/stack cases. `code.slice(0, MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE)` could be deleted with the suite still green.

The 'request paths pin every id to one segment' suite in upstream-error.test.ts exercises `deleteDocument`, `setCell`, `renameTab`, the configured workspace and the dot-segment refusal, but never `downloadFileDocument`. The behavioural delta of this change on that method is precisely the dot-segment throw (encoding was already there), and no test asserts `downloadFileDocument('..')` throws rather than issuing a walked-up request.
searchedFor: packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts ('request paths pin every id to one segment')

samples.summary: `isTimeout`'s `AbortError` branch and `collectAndEmbedImages`' injectable `onImageError` are each untested
samples.evidence: The multi-address fallback suite throws only `new DOMException(..., 'TimeoutError')` ('does not retry other addresses after a timeout'); the `name === 'AbortError'` arm is never hit. Similarly, `collectAndEmbedImages`' new `onImageError` parameter is only ever exercised through its `warnImageError` default (pdf-exporter.test.ts spies on console.warn); no test injects a custom reporter.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (3) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding contains no defect claim about this repository — its text is verbatim the harness's own runtime failure record. `poolExhaustedError()` at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 emits "<label>: every credential in the pool (N) was retired — nothing left to fail over to", and `lensFailureSummary()` at scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1651-1656 prefixes it with "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: ". The item therefore reports that the review lens's credential pool drained mid-run and it never produced a verdict; it names no file, no test, and no behavior. There is no code "present as described" to evaluate — refutation ground `not-present`. Additionally, on the most charitable reading (that the pool-exhaustion path itself lacks coverage), that reading also fails: scripts/agent/ask.test.mjs:295-308 asserts the error's message/kind/retryable and that no upstream prose leaks; 310-326 drives the real `askStructured` against a drained pool through the `__setTokenPool` seam; 328-349 verifies `failoverStep` reports the pool rather than the last slot and leaves non-credential errors untouched; 351-361 verifies an all-bad pool drains and stops. These are non-vacuous and would fail if the logic broke. scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1645-1649 documents that infra failures are explicitly not code findings. Nothing here is a vacuous test, an untested behavior change, or over-mocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
